topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning objectives for the session on cancer causation.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Risk: Genetics, Endogenous Mutations, and Environmental Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer etiology, contrasting endogenous processes and genetic predisposition with external environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Specific Carcinogens, Pathogens, and Tumor Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific physical, chemical, and biological agents and the cellular mechanisms—including metabolic activation, direct DNA damage, tissue susceptibility, and promotional inflammation—by which they drive carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, toxicological, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposures and establish causal links to cancer.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the concluding lecture remarks, summarising key themes on cancer causation and addressing everyday risk-benefit decision-making.
